Title: Philippines ex-leader Duterte makes first appearance at ICC
Article:
THE HAGUE: Former Philippines president Rodrigo Duterte appeared in person at the International Criminal Court for the first time Wednesday, as he faces charges over his "war on drugs" that killed thousands.
The 81-year-old had appeared by videolink when he was first brought to the court in The Hague, but had since skipped various hearings, with his defence team claiming he was too ill.
Dressed in a dark suit and white shirt with no tie, the former president sat with his chin resting on his hands as the proceedings opened.
Judge Joanna Korner noted his appearance in court for the first time, and said he could leave the court at any time without seeking permission from the bench.
Duterte faces three counts of crimes against humanity, with prosecutors alleging his involvement in at least 76 murders between 2013 and 2018 during his offensive against drug users and sellers.
He is the first Asian former head of state to face trial at the ICC, which prosecutes individuals for the world's worst crimes such as war crimes and crimes against humanity.
Judge Korner has set November 30 as the start date of the trial, which could take months or even years.
Wednesday's hearing was a "status hearing" for the parties and the judge to fix logistical details.
The only time Duterte had been seen since his arrest in March 2025 was an initial appearance via video, where he seemed confused and tired, his speech barely audible.
His defence team has argued he is not mentally fit to follow proceedings and that his condition continues to deteriorate.
In a submission published on Tuesday, Duterte's defence team said he suffered from "significant memory impairment that prevents him from retaining recent information and reliably accessing memories."
Judges are weighing whether he is mentally fit to be tried and have ordered a medical assessment by three experts.
That assessment has not been made public but Duterte's defence cited the results of examinations contained in the report.
According to the defence, these examination showed Duterte thinks he is living in 2007 or 2008, that he is 84 or 85 years old, and could not recall the name of the current US president.
During "confirmation of charges" hearings in February, the prosecution alleged Duterte killed thousands of suspected drug dealers and users, first as mayor of Davao City, then as president.
"Decades of murdering his own people, murdering the children of the Philippines, and he claims that he did it all for his country. He doesn't deny it," said Julian Nicholls, summing up for the prosecution after the hearings.
"He ran a death squad in Davao that he created," said Nicholls, referring to the city where he was mayor before he became president.
"His promise was to kill thousands and he did."
The true number of killings during his campaign in the Philippines is thought to be in the thousands, and lawyers for the victims have argued that a full trial could encourage more families to come forward.
His then defence lawyer Nicolas Kaufman told the court in February that his client "absolutely" maintained his innocence.
Kaufman told ICC judges the evidence against Duterte was "wholly insufficient" and the charges "grievously misplaced and politically motivated."
He argued that while Duterte used "bluster and hyperbole" in his speeches, he also frequently ordered authorities only to shoot in self-defence.
Duterte remains popular in the Philippines, where many favoured his tough approach to crime.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cable thieves caught on video in Jalan Jelatek, RM15,000 in losses reported
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are investigating an attempted cable theft in Jalan Jelatek, Datuk Keramat, which allegedly caused losses estimated at RM15,000.
Ampang Jaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid said a report was lodged after a company representative received a video of the incident at 4.30pm yesterday.
He said the video, which was shared on social media, showed several people allegedly pulling cables belonging to a telecommunications company.
"They were seen using a white four-wheel-drive vehicle and a white Toyota Harrier. The registration numbers could not be ascertained.
"The company estimated its losses at about RM15,000 and a police report was subsequently lodged for further action," he said in a statement today.
Khairul Anuar said police had also detected the video circulating on Threads.
He said the case was being investigated under Sections 379, 431A and 124K of the Penal Code, as well as Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
Section 379, which covers theft, carries a jail term of up to seven years, a fine, or both upon conviction.
Section 431A provides for imprisonment of up to two years, a fine, or both, while Section 124K carries a jail term of up to 40 years, a fine, or both.
An offence under Section 233 carries a maximum one-year jail term, a fine of up to RM50,000, or both, upon conviction.

Title: Cabinet ministers call for unity, respect on Malaysia Day
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Cabinet ministers have called on Malaysians to uphold unity, mutual respect and appreciation of diversity as the foundations of national strength and ensure that progress and prosperity are enjoyed by all.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Malaysia Day served as a reminder that the country was built on mutual understanding, unity and a shared determination to move forward together.
"Malaysia's formation is not the story of a single state, territory or group. It is our shared story, from the peninsula to Sabah and Sarawak.
"In the spirit of Segulai Sejalai, let us continue to honour our history, safeguard unity and ensure that all Malaysians benefit from the country's progress and prosperity," he said in a Facebook post.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said Malaysia's peace and harmony stemmed from the sacrifices of previous generations and the sustained efforts of all Malaysians.
He said differences in race, religion, culture and background were not obstacles but a source of strength and part of the country's identity.
"Our responsibility today is to preserve what has been built, respect one another and strengthen unity among Malaysians," he said.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said being Malaysian was not merely an identity but a shared responsibility to safeguard peace, preserve harmony and defend the country's sovereignty.
"A strong Malaysia is not built by itself. It is built by people who stand united, trust one another and remain committed to the country. May the unity we have forged continue to be a source of strength for Malaysia," he said.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan urged Malaysians to strengthen solidarity and mutual respect while working together to build a more progressive, inclusive and prosperous Malaysia Madani.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said Malaysia Day reaffirmed the commitment to building a healthy, prosperous and inclusive nation, with everyone entitled to fair, equitable and quality healthcare.
Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said unity must be reflected in justice, mutual respect and equitable development, including better public wellbeing, food security and the welfare of farmers, rice farmers, fishermen and livestock breeders.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri called for stronger ties between Sabah, Sarawak and the peninsula through mutual respect, understanding and cooperation.
Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing said Malaysia's diverse cultures, languages, customs and heritage were part of the country's rich identity.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi also called for the spirit of Malaysia Day to continue bringing Malaysians together in building a peaceful, progressive and prosperous future.
Others who extended Malaysia Day greetings included Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo, Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang, Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad, and Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup.

Title: AI ambition needs smarter computing, not just more power
Article:
LETTER:
The current excitement around artificial intelligence can create the impression that more computing power automatically produces better innovation. That is not necessarily true.
The more complex solution is not automatically the better one. The appropriate solution depends on the problem, the quality of the data, the level of accuracy required and the consequences of making a mistake.
Good data, basic analytics and appropriate visualisation may already provide the insight required.
Responsible AI therefore includes knowing when not to use the largest AI system available.
I believe our students need to understand that good software is not merely software that works. Good computing should also be efficient.
When two algorithms solve the same problem, which one requires fewer operations? When should data be processed locally rather than repeatedly transferred to distant servers?
When is a smaller AI model sufficient? How can a database be designed so that unnecessary processing is reduced?
Future technology professionals will therefore need to think about more than functionality. They will need to think about computational efficiency.
Infrastructure alone does not make Malaysia an advanced digital economy.
People do. Malaysia will need professionals in cloud computing, networking, cybersecurity, software engineering, data engineering, artificial intelligence and high performance computing plus mathematicians, statisticians and data analysts.
The AI economy is often described as if it belongs only to programmers.
In reality, mathematics and statistics are fundamental to optimisation, machine learning, forecasting and evidence based decision making.
This is why universities and faculties of computing and mathematical sciences should be closely connected to the development of Malaysia's data centre ecosystem.
Students should understand not only how to use an AI application, but how data moves through a system, how models consume computing resources, how networks carry information and how infrastructure must be secured.
The long term objective should be to transform infrastructure investment into national technological capability.
Malaysia's AI ambitions are worth pursuing.
The country has an opportunity to build digital infrastructure, attract investment and develop expertise that could support economic growth for decades.
The goal should not simply be to have more servers, larger models or greater computing capacity.
Our aim should be to produce more value from every unit of computing power we use and understand how to use it wisely.
ABD MALIK MOHD RICK
Senior Lecturer
Faculty of Computer and Mathematical Sciences
Universiti Teknologi MARA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar condemns drone threat near Makkah, urges restraint
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has condemned the reported drone threat near Makkah, saying any attempt to endanger the safety and sanctity of Islam's holiest city is unacceptable.
Anwar said Malaysia appreciated the swift action taken by Saudi Arabia to protect residents and pilgrims in Makkah.
"I view with grave concern reports that a drone was intercepted near Makkah. Any attempt to threaten the safety and sanctity of Islam's holiest city would be wholly unacceptable," he said in a statement today.
He said the incident highlighted the urgent need to prevent further escalation in the region, calling for an immediate end to attacks on civilian sites and any actions that could endanger holy sites.
"We urge the relevant parties to exercise restraint and pursue a peaceful resolution through dialogue without delay," he said.
Earlier, Saudi Arabia issued
emergency alerts
warning of a "potential danger" in Jeddah, Makkah and Taif, urging residents to seek shelter and follow official safety instructions, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
The alerts were issued through the National Early Warning Platform for Emergencies, according to Saudi Civil Defence.
The alerts came amid escalating clashes between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi group, which has carried out a series of missile and drone attacks on Saudi cities and infrastructure in recent days. Saudi forces have responded with strikes on Houthi positions in Yemen.
Meanwhile, Malaysians in Jeddah and Makkah were reported
safe
following the emergency alert issued by Saudi authorities yesterday.
Malaysian Consul-General in Jeddah Tengku Mohd Dzaraif Raja Abdul Kadir said the consulate had circulated an official graphic issued by the Saudi Arabian Ministry of Interior through WhatsApp groups for Malaysians in the Hijaz region.

Title: English village votes to 'secede' from UK over asylum centre plan
Article:
LONDON: An English village of around 350 people announced Wednesday that a vast majority of residents had voted yes in an "independence referendum" staged to protest plans to house over 1,200 migrants in a nearby facility.
Piddington in central England, 25 kilometres from the university city of Oxford, has grabbed headlines with its tongue-in-cheek breakaway vote.
The village's parish council announced that with 312 ballots counted, 285 had voted to secede from Britain over plans to house asylum seekers in a nearby disused military site, in a symbolic vote with no recognised legal basis.
Residents were handed a ballot paper with the statement: "I support Piddington seeking to secede from the United Kingdom and pursuing self-determination."
The local parish council chair Tim McNally said that the village will now be known as the "principality of Piddington."
McNally told Sky News: "For us, it's about proportionality – how does a small village of 350 odd people assimilate with 1,250 males?"
He accused the government of "trying to rush this whole plan through."
"I think what this result shows is that Piddington campaigners have done an incredible job to highlight their concerns about the proposed asylum centre," the leader of Oxfordshire county council, Tim Bearder, told the BBC.
The council chief warned the planned centre "will be a lightning rod to the far right, who come here to protest" and "potentially attack" asylum seekers.
But Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy told the BBC that a former military base "is a better option for housing asylum seekers" than hotels or rented accommodation.
"We do have to house people somewhere while we get a grip on the asylum chaos... and that base will go ahead," she said.
[[nid:1534097]]
Around Britain, regular protests have been staged in towns and villages against the housing of asylum seekers in hotels and other facilities.
The Piddington referendum was a play on the British comedy film "Passport to Pimlico."
In the 1949 classic, a small group of Londoners discover treasure and declare independence making them exempt from post-war rationing and other bureaucratic restrictions.
"I voted to leave the United Kingdom," 76-year-old Piddington resident Herbert Owen, told AFP during the vote, saying it felt like the government did not "care" about the bucolic village in the Oxfordshire countryside.
"We have a village hall, a 12th-century church and a playing field – and that's it," another villager Ian Darby, 63, said, questioning how the migrants would spend their time.
"It is a takeover of our village, it's four times the people of this village. They are going to want to get out and about (locally) and that raises serious issues," he said.
"I've lived here, my whole life... I won't really feel safe enough to walk around anymore," 17-year-old student and part-time stablehand Dita Jackson told AFP.
According to the government, the proposed centre would be used for a minimum of 10 years to house single adult male asylum seekers.
The "safety and security" of the migrants, staff at the base and the local community would be "of the utmost importance", it said.
The centre-left Labour Party, in power since July 2024, is phasing out the use of hotels as migrant accommodation, a policy it inherited from the previous Conservative government.
It has vowed to completely end their use by the end of this parliament, due in 2029, turning instead to ex-military bases.

Title: Anwar calls for shared progress on Malaysia Day
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said no region or community should be left behind in the country's development.
He said Malaysia Day should serve as a renewed commitment to national unity and shared progress.
Anwar said Sept 16 should remind Malaysians that the country was built on a bond between the government and the people, the regions and the Federation, as well as loyalty and justice.
"We must acknowledge that there have been times when the country's journey strayed, when racial issues were exploited, regional disparities were allowed to widen, and differences were turned into walls and dividing lines," he said in a Facebook post.
Anwar said the commitment must be renewed constantly to ensure no region was regarded as marginalised, no community felt isolated and no Malaysian was left behind.
The South China Sea might separate Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak geographically, he said, but it should not divide their shared aspirations for the nation.
"The sea may separate us, but not our national aspirations and hopes," he said.
Anwar said Malaysia's diversity should instead be viewed as a source of strength and a foundation for building a more united country.
He said the spirit of Malaysia Day required all regions and communities to share in the country's development and ensure the benefits of progress reached Malaysians regardless of where they lived.
"Happy Malaysia Day!" he added.

Title: Wife attack: Man with 27 criminal, drug offence cases arrested
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A man with 27 previous records involving criminal and drug offences has been arrested for allegedly assaulting and slashing his wife with a sharp weapon in an incident believed to have been linked to jealousy.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the unemployed man, in his late 20s, was detained at the compound of the Dang Wangi district police headquarters on Sept 8.
"Acting on information, a team from the Cheras district police Criminal Investigation Division (D7) arrested the local man at the compound of the Dang Wangi district police headquarters on Sept 8," Fadil said in a statement today.
The suspect's previous records comprised 15 criminal cases and 12 offences under the Dangerous Drugs Act.
A urine screening also tested positive for drugs.
The victim, a woman in her 40s, was admitted to the orthopaedic ward at Hospital Ampang after the attack.
A doctor at the hospital lodged a police report on Aug 29 after treating the woman.
She lodged her own report on Sept 4 after being discharged.
Jealousy was believed to have been behind the incident.
Fadil said the suspect was remanded for six days until Sept 14 to facilitate investigations before being released on police bail the same day.
"The case is being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt using a weapon.
"The offence carries a maximum jail term of 10 years, a fine, whipping, or any two of the punishments upon conviction," he said.

Title: China opens major canal linking landlocked regions to sea
Article:
BEIJING: China opened a major canal on Wednesday that will provide landlocked areas with direct access to the sea, state media said, reducing transport times and costs as the country aims to bolster trade ties with regional neighbours.
The 134-kilometre Pinglu Canal took four years to build and links Nanning, in the southern manufacturing region of Guangxi, to the Gulf of Tonkin, flanked by China and Vietnam.
Goods from southwestern China previously had to be transported to the southern metropolis of Guangzhou in order to reach the sea, but the new canal will cut the journey by more than 560 kilometres, state news agency Xinhua said.
The canal will also reduce transport costs by 18 to 30 per cent, and generate annual savings of more than five billion yuan (US$745 million) in the sector, it added.
State broadcaster CCTV broadcast footage of the first barge to pass through the canal and aerial video of ships navigating its calm waters, describing the waterway as "the project of our century."
The canal "opens up the shortest, most economical and most convenient route" to Southeast Asia and will boost economic development, Xinhua said.
The new route is particularly important to rural parts of Sichuan, Chongqing and Yunnan, among others, which are less well-connected than more prosperous regions in eastern China.
Coal, ore, cereals, chemicals, agricultural produce and other materials will now be able to reach foreign markets more easily.
The bulk of the canal's construction work involved widening, deepening and modifying existing waterways, while a small section had to be excavated, Xinhua said.
The project, which began in August 2022, cost a total of 72.7 billion yuan, it added.

Title: Policeman injured chasing cable theft suspects in Kluang
Article:
KLUANG: A policeman was injured after falling from his motorcycle while pursuing a group of men suspected of stealing cables in Jalan Dorset here early today.
Kluang deputy police chief Superintendent Nik Mohd Azmi Husin said police received a report at 5.45am that a motorcycle patrol officer had been injured and immediately rushed to the scene.
"The district police headquarters confirmed receiving a report that the patrol officer was injured after falling while pursuing suspects believed to be involved in cable theft, as seen in a video that went viral on social media.
"Investigations found that the cable theft occurred at 1.57am, with the suspects using a Mitsubishi four-wheel-drive vehicle to tow the cables," he said.
Police are still tracking down the suspects, and the case is being investigated under Section 379 of the Penal Code for theft and Section 353 of the same law for using criminal force to deter or prevent a public servant from carrying out his duties.
Those with information can contact the Kluang district police headquarters at 07-7784222, 07-7766822 (hotline), 07-7784256 or 014-365682.
Earlier, a video went viral showing a group of men using a pickup truck to tow cables behind the vehicle before fleeing the scene.
The incident was reportedly recorded by members of the public.
Comments on social media also called for stern action against those involved in cable theft.
One social media user, Muhammad Redzwan Sam, said cables being dragged along roads could pose a danger to other road users and disrupt public safety.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johari backs DRB-HICOM, Proton push into India's auto sector
Article:
NEW DELHI: Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani has backed DRB-HICOM Bhd and Proton Holdings Bhd's efforts to explore opportunities in India's automotive industry.
This includes the potential use of the group's Tanjung Malim manufacturing capabilities in Perak to supply components or establish partnerships with Indian automotive players.
Johari said DRB-HICOM was exploring ways to leverage its manufacturing and automotive capabilities in Malaysia to participate directly in India.
This includes component supply, technology and engineering cooperation or joint ventures with local industry players.
"I believe DRB-HICOM has just started to explore this," he told the New Straits Times after the conclusion of the 18th BRICS summit, here on Sept 13.
"As the Investment, Trade and Industry Minister, I would certainly give full support to DRB-HICOM to explore its capacity in Tanjung Malim as one of the plants that can be directly involved in its efforts to participate in the automotive industry in India," the minister said.
The move comes as Malaysia seeks to deepen industrial cooperation with India and encourage Malaysian companies to tap the country's large consumer market and established automotive ecosystem.
Johari said the opportunity should not be viewed solely as an attempt to export finished vehicles but as a broader industrial play involving automotive components, manufacturing, technology and potential partnerships with Indian companies.
For DRB-HICOM, the Tanjung Malim complex provides an increasingly integrated manufacturing and technology base.
Proton has consolidated its manufacturing and R&D operations there, while its powertrain facility produces engines, transmissions and electric drive units for current and future vehicles.
Johari said DRB-HICOM could potentially use these capabilities as a platform to develop partnerships with Indian automotive companies and participate in the country's wider automotive supply chain.
"There is a lot of work in progress for Proton to emerge as a player in India's automotive market," he said.
The latest exploration marks a renewed look at India by Proton, which has previously studied opportunities in the market but has never established a commercial manufacturing or sales presence there.
During the BRICS Summit, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said DRB-HICOM and potential Indian industry partners had discussed opportunities.
However, no decision has been announced on a local plant, distributor, vehicle line-up or launch timetable.
India's scale adds to the attraction.
Passenger-vehicle registrations reached about 412,000 units in July 2026, up 15.4 per cent from a year earlier, according to JATO Dynamics India, with SUVs continuing to account for a significant share of demand.
For Proton, India could also provide an opportunity to extend its international expansion as the company builds its export business and develops electric and next-generation vehicles.
Proton recorded 6,000 export units in 2025, its highest export volume since 2012, while sales momentum continued into 2026.
In the first eight months of the year, Proton sold a total of 141,421 vehicles, up about 40 per cent year-on-year, driven in part by growing demand for its electrified models.
In August alone Proton sold 22,632 vehicles globally, its highest monthly sales performance since January 2010.
Johari said Malaysia's broader objective was to use India's huge market to create a more balanced two-way trading relationship, rather than simply increasing Malaysian exports.
His comments followed discussions with India's Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Malaysia's sizeable trade surplus with India and the need to expand two-way trade.
Johari said both countries were looking at ways to strengthen their trade framework, including potentially finalising or revising the existing free trade agreement within the next three to six months.
He said India's population of about 1.4 billion to 1.5 billion offered Malaysian companies a substantial market, while partnerships with Indian companies could allow Malaysian businesses to participate more deeply in the country's domestic economy.
"As a small nation, we want to see how we can work together with India, which has a huge population, and create a win-win situation between both nations instead of a one-way relationship," he said.
For DRB-HICOM, that strategy could extend beyond Proton-branded vehicles to components, engineering, manufacturing, technology and mobility solutions, potentially giving the group multiple entry points into India's automotive value chain.
The exploration also comes as DRB-HICOM develops Tanjung Malim as a broader automotive and next-generation vehicle hub.
The group has been positioning the Automotive High-Tech Valley as an ecosystem encompassing R&D, manufacturing, logistics and supporting automotive services.
Johari said the government would support efforts by Malaysian companies to use domestic industrial capabilities as a springboard for greater participation in large overseas markets.
"We cannot only trade with one or two countries. We want to trade with all countries, especially those with huge populations," he said.

Title: A-G: Muhyiddin still faces three Jana Wibawa charges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar has stressed that the three charges against former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin linked to the Jana Wibawa programme are still being pursued in court.
Dusuki said the decision not to proceed with four charges against Muhyiddin involved Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and was unrelated to the Jana Wibawa charges.
"There has been a lot of misunderstanding. The Bukhary Equity case has nothing to do with Jana Wibawa. We are continuing with the Jana Wibawa case.
"I am not responding specifically to any party, but explaining the matter generally," he said when contacted today.
His remarks followed calls by DAP chairman Gobind Singh Deo for an explanation over the prosecution's decision to seek a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) before the High Court which ultimately granted Muhyiddin a discharge amounting to an acquittal (DAA) on the four charges.
Gobind, who is also Digital Minister, said transparency was important as the high-profile trial had reached its final stages.
The Attorney-General's Chambers (
A-GC
) said in a statement yesterday that the decision not to proceed with the four charges linked to Bukhary Equity was based on a professional assessment of the evidence, the evidential viability of the case and the overall interests of the prosecution.
The A-GC said the decision did not mean the charges had been brought without basis, nor could it be interpreted as a finding that the transactions under investigation had not taken place.
It added that prosecutorial decisions could and should be reviewed after considering the entirety and admissibility of the evidence, witness credibility and implications for other proceedings.
The High Court yesterday discharged and acquitted Muhyiddin of one charge of using his position to obtain
RM200 million
in gratification and three money-laundering charges involving the same amount.
Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin made the order after allowing the prosecution's application not to proceed with the four charges related to Bukhary Equity.
The prosecution subsequently closed its case in the Jana Wibawa trial after calling 29 witnesses.
Muhyiddin, 79, still faces three charges of using his position to obtain RM25.3 million in gratification for Bersatu from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Mamfor Sdn Bhd and KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, as well as its director Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, in connection with the Jana Wibawa projects.
He is alleged to have committed the offences at the Prime Minister's Office, Bangunan Perdana Putra, Putrajaya, between March 1, 2020 and Aug 20, 2021, under Section 23(1) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009.

Title: Malaysia among economies positioned to capture upside as Asean growth paths diverge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is among the Southeast Asian economies positioned to capture disproportionate upside over the next decade, according to a report by Bain & Company, DBS Bank and Vriens & Partners.
This is amid stronger investment flows, industrial expansion and technology adoption reshaping the region's growth outlook.
The report, "From Tailwinds to Trade-Offs: Southeast Asia Outlook 2026-2035", projects Southeast Asia's six largest economies - Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam - to grow by an average of 4.8 per cent annually between 2026 and 2035.
While the regional growth outlook remains broadly intact, the report said economic trajectories are diverging.
Institutional strength, energy security and technological readiness increasingly determine each country's ability to withstand shocks and benefit from new opportunities.
Malaysia, Singapore and Vietnam are identified as economies that could capture greater upside under more favourable conditions.
This will be supported by their exposure to manufacturing exports, semiconductor demand and investment momentum.
The report noted that the Asean-6 economies recorded average growth of 5.1 per cent in 2024 and 2025, in line with the previous outlook's projection.
However, performance varied significantly, with Vietnam expanding 7.5 per cent over the two-year period compared with Thailand's 2.7 per cent.
Malaysia's position reflects its role in regional manufacturing and supply chains, particularly as global companies diversify production and investment amid the intensifying US-China rivalry and ongoing supply-chain realignment.
The report said net foreign direct investment inflows into the Asean-6 rose 25 per cent in 2025, even as inflows into China contracted 34 per cent.
This underscores Southeast Asia's growing role in global investment and manufacturing networks.
However, the report cautioned that investment and export gains - driven increasingly by electronics and AI infrastructure - have yet to translate into broad-based productivity improvements across the region.
For Malaysia, the challenge will be to convert its position in high-value manufacturing and electrical and electronics supply chains into stronger domestic capabilities, higher productivity and wider economic spillovers.
The report also highlighted the importance of energy security, reliable infrastructure and policy execution in determining whether economies can attract and retain high-quality investments.
The report identified three priorities that will increasingly influence Malaysia's and the region's economic performance: strengthening institutional resilience, fortifying energy systems and capturing the AI dividend.
Institutional resilience, including governance, the rule of law, fiscal stability and deeper capital markets, is becoming more important in sustaining investor confidence and ensuring effective policy execution.
Energy systems must also be strengthened through reliable grids, diversified import sources and bankable renewable-energy projects, particularly as industrial expansion and AI-related infrastructure increase electricity demand.
Meanwhile, countries that move beyond AI pilot projects towards enterprise-scale adoption are expected to capture greater productivity gains, provided they invest in data governance, computing infrastructure and workforce development.
The report said Southeast Asia's 4.8 per cent baseline growth forecast remains achievable, but it is not automatic.
Domestic policy decisions over the next two to three years will determine whether economies convert current tailwinds into durable competitive advantages.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Losing mother in prison was 'most painful' moment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has described the night his mother died while he was in prison as one of the most painful and difficult moments of his life.
Anwar said being behind bars and unable to do anything as his beloved mother took her final breath was an immense ordeal.
"That night was indeed the most painful night for me. Imagine your beloved mother returning to the mercy of Allah while you are confined to a prison cell.
"I could do nothing except pray, read the Quran and offer prayers. The following day, I was allowed to leave to go home and perform the funeral prayers," he said while appearing as a guest on the Sembang OhhYeahh podcast.
Recalling the episode, Anwar said he was informed about his mother's deteriorating condition by his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
"My wife told me that my mother was critically ill. At that point, I pleaded to be allowed to see her, even if only briefly.
"Eventually, after making repeated appeals, I was told I could see her for about half an hour at the hospital. My mother was critically ill but conscious and very happy. I then returned to prison, and shortly afterwards, she died," he said.
Anwar said while losing a parent was difficult for anyone, the loss of a mother had a deeper emotional impact on him than losing his father.
"Losing a mother is much more difficult than losing a father. Losing a father is difficult, but it is not the same as losing a mother," he said.
Apart from recalling his mother's death, Anwar also spoke about the hardships he endured while in detention, including being beaten unconscious on his first day in prison.
However, he said he never gave up because he was mindful of the younger generation and his struggle to bring about change and save the country from corruption and oppression.
"This struggle is not easy and comes at a high price. If I give up, the entire generation will be left behind," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 129 still missing four days after capsize of ship in Indonesia's Java Sea
Article:
BANJARMASIN: Desperation and frustration are growing among families of the 129 people still missing following the weekend capsizing of a ship in Indonesia's Java Sea, as persistent heavy seas and bad weather continue to restrict search-and-rescue operations.
The Virgo Transport 8 was carrying 243 people on a 20-hour voyage from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan when it capsized in bad weather early on Sunday.
On Wednesday, the official death toll stood at six people with 108 rescued and 129 unaccounted for, tallies that have not changed since Sunday.
"I hope we would use our advanced military equipment, we buy them to help people, right? Or else what for? For war? We likely will not go to war,"  said 37-year-old Fauzi, who has been waiting for news of seven family members, including his mother, who were on the ship.
Fauzi, who goes by one name, said that after four days of waiting at the rescue command centre in Banjarmasin for promised updates about the search, his hopes have begun to fade.
"We do not hope much but what we need is certainty," he said.
The Coast Guard and Navy have been unable to launch underwater search-and-rescue operations because of waves of up to 2.5 metres and strong winds near the capsized vessel, I Putu Sudayana, the head of Banjarmasin's rescue agency, told Reuters.
On Wednesday, six ships were deployed for a surface search, Putu said, along with helicopters and aircraft.
Maria Dethan, 21, has stayed in the command centre since it was set up, anxiously waiting for news of her brother Samuel.
"Every time I am about to eat, I always remember my brother because I believe he has been starving for days," she told Reuters, saying she needed some certainty from authorities.
"I hope there will be clear information about my brother today," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia-Australia defence ties set for deeper strategic cooperation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia-Australia defence ties are set to deepen following Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin's working visit to Australia, with both sides looking to pursue more strategic, substantive and outcome-oriented cooperation.
Khaled, who arrived in Melbourne today, will begin the visit with a meeting with the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation (ASIO) to exchange views on current security developments and challenges of mutual interest.
He will then travel to Geelong for a courtesy call and bilateral meeting with Australian Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Richard Marles.
"The meeting will focus on the development of bilateral defence relations as well as new areas that can be explored together.
"The highlight of the visit will be the sixth Malaysia-Australia High-Level Committee (HLC) Meeting on Friday, which I will co-chair with Marles," he said in a statement.
Khaled said the meeting, following last year's gathering in Kuala Lumpur, would assess progress in defence cooperation, explore new opportunities and chart the future direction of bilateral defence ties.
"Malaysia and Australia have long-standing defence relations and cooperation, spanning times of war and peace, and continuing to develop through bilateral and multilateral cooperation.
"The foundation of this strong relationship is the mutual trust and confidence built by both countries over many years," he said.
He said Malaysia and Australia also worked closely through platforms such as the Five Power Defence Arrangements (FPDA) and Asean Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) to address regional security challenges.
Khaled said that amid an increasingly complex security landscape, long-standing ties must continue to be strengthened and elevated from cooperation towards more strategic, substantive and outcome-oriented collaboration.
Accompanying Khaled on the visit are Defence Ministry deputy secretary-general (policy) Datuk Mohd Yani Daud, Malaysian High Commissioner to Australia Datin Paduka Sharrina Abdullah, Malaysia Defence Intelligence Organisation director-general Lieutenant-General Datuk Fazal Abdul Rahman, and senior ministry and armed forces officers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia prioritises diplomacy over compensation in addressing transboundary haze, says Zahid
Article:
KUCHING: Malaysia prioritises long-term diplomatic cooperation and early preventive measures over seeking compensation from neighbouring countries in addressing transboundary haze.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is also the National Disaster Management Committee chairman, said a prudent and structured diplomatic approach is the most effective way to address sensitive issues among Asean member states while ensuring optimal technical coordination.
"While seeking compensation does not necessarily imply definitive liability that must be borne by any specific country, taking preventive measures early would avoid the need to address such sensitive inter-state issues.
"Diplomatic measures must be pursued alongside technical efforts involving officials from neighbouring countries and Malaysian states," he told a press conference after chairing the First National Disaster Management High-Level Committee Meeting of 2026 at Wisma Bapa Malaysia here today.
He was responding to a question on whether Malaysia intended to raise the issue of losses suffered by the country, particularly regarding the economy, health, and tourism, as a result of transboundary haze with the Indonesian government.
Also present were Sarawak Deputy Premier and Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas, and deputy Rural and Regional Development minister Datuk Rubiah Wang.
Meanwhile, Zahid, who is also the Rural and Regional Development Minister, said the transboundary haze issue will be officially raised during his working visit to Jakarta from tomorrow until Sept 20 in conjunction with the Halal-20 Conference: 5th World Halal Summit 2026.
"That is among the topics to be discussed with the Minister of Environment or the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability minister in the Malaysian context.
"There are seven ministers who will be holding discussions with me, covering other areas such as the halal sector and so forth.
"A key topic I will discuss and coordinate with Bapak Gibran is the haze problem," he said, referring to Indonesian Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka.
Regarding assistance to neighbouring countries, Zahid said the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) had been directed to stand ready to coordinate cloud seeding operations and logistical support to help tackle forest and peatland fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, should an official request be received.
Meanwhile, in a statement issued following the meeting, Zahid said the government is shifting towards an "anticipatory action" approach to address the threat of extreme hot and dry weather caused by Super El Niño.
The measures include hotspot monitoring, ensuring the readiness of firefighting assets, peatland management, enforcement against open burning, and disseminating health information to the public.
"The Department of Minerals and Geoscience Malaysia and the Department of Environment have been asked to evaluate the use of tube wells as an alternative water source, including refurbishing existing infrastructure in high-risk areas," he said.
According to the statement, the National Disaster Management Council had also approved an allocation of RM5 million this year for cloud seeding operations and related management, comprising RM2 million for Phase One approved on June 2, and RM3 million for Phase Two approved on Sept 2.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar to invite Myanmar president, push for Rohingya repatriation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will invite Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing to make an official visit to Malaysia as part of efforts to expedite the repatriation of Rohingya refugees.
Anwar said the move was aimed at finding a long-term solution to the issue, which has increasingly sparked concern among locals.
"Two weeks ago, I told the Home Ministry and cabinet members that I would invite the Myanmar president to make an official visit to Malaysia.
"Why? To tell them that we can be friends and trade. We can accept Myanmar, but they must take back the refugees. If they cannot take all 200,000 at once, then do it in stages.
"We will help to solve this. This is my way of solving it, through diplomacy," he said in the Sembang Ohh Yeahh podcast, which aired today.
Anwar also criticised politicians whom he said were exploiting the issue.
"I understand the people's anger. They are facing difficulties, including finding jobs, and Rohingya refugees can sometimes be aggressive.
"But as leaders, we can be angry, but what does that achieve? The solution is to negotiate with the Myanmar government to secure its agreement for them to be repatriated.
"So far, they have agreed to take back 5,000, with 1,500 to be repatriated within the next one to two weeks.
"If we do not do this, it will become a burden in terms of security and the economy, as well as create hostility among the people," he said.
Anwar said Malaysia's good relations with Myanmar provided room for the country to push for the refugees' repatriation.
He said this was preferable to Malaysia bearing the cost of providing food and other necessities for hundreds of thousands of refugees held at detention depots.
"Some suggest that we arrest them, but after arresting them, where are we going to put them?" he said, adding that Malaysia incurred substantial costs in managing refugees at detention depots.
Anwar also said the large number of Rohingya refugees in Malaysia was partly linked to actions by previous administrations, which had organised large-scale gatherings to welcome their arrival.
"In the past, the previous government invited them. There were large gatherings in support of them, with speeches by prominent government figures at the time.
"Now, because of the influx, I am the one being blamed for bringing these people in," he said.
On July 29, Anwar said Myanmar had agreed to accept an
initial group of 5,000 Rohingya
from Malaysia following negotiations between the two governments.
He said the move was part of broader efforts to address the long-running Rohingya issue while maintaining public order in Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Young Curators' turns museums into classrooms for 2,373 students
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Rather than simply viewing artefacts behind glass, 2,373 students were given the chance to step into the shoes of curators through the 'Bermalam di Muzium' (Night at the Museum) 2026 programme.
Themed 'Young Curators', the programme was held at 32 museums nationwide to encourage young people to learn about, appreciate and preserve the country's heritage.
National Unity Ministry deputy secretary-general (Policy and Strategic Planning) Mohamad Sobri Mat Daud said the initiative was important in ensuring history was not confined to the classroom, but could be experienced first-hand through museum collections and artefacts.
"When they visit museums, what they learn at school can be experienced first-hand through the artefacts, while also fostering closer ties among students of various races.
"We want to foster closer ties, build students' identity and self-confidence. By learning about the country's artefacts and civilisation, they will develop a greater love for the country while further strengthening the bonds of unity among one another. That is our aspiration," he told reporters after the programme's closing ceremony at Dataran Muzium Negara here today.
Also present were Museums Department (JMM) deputy director-general (Policy) Mohamad Shawali Badi, JMM deputy director-general (Museums) Mohd Razaimi Hamat, Akademi Kenegaraan Malaysia (AKM) deputy director-general (Management) Saliza Mokhtar, and National Museum director Zamrul Amri Zakaria.
Sobri said the exposure could help shape the younger generation into future leaders with a strong sense of identity and patriotic spirit.
Meanwhile, Shawali said the 'Young Curators' theme gave students an insight into the work involved in preserving the country's heritage.
He said curators were responsible for various museum activities, including research, preservation, collection management and exhibitions.
"By understanding the role of curators, we hope students will better appreciate the efforts undertaken by museums, not only as places that store historical artefacts, but also as institutions that preserve and impart knowledge to the public," he said.
The two-day programme, held from Sept 15 to 16, featured activities including the Young Curators programme, a talk by AKM, knowledge-sharing sessions with curators, the Young Curators Fun Walk and Museum Exploration.
The programme was organised in collaboration with the National Unity Ministry, JMM, the Education Ministry, educational institutions, state and institutional museums, and strategic partners including AKM, Yayasan MR DIY, Thong Bowl and Yeos.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Smuggled cigarettes hidden beneath concrete piles seized at Tuas
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An attempt to smuggle 4,500 cartons of duty-unpaid cigarettes into Singapore using a Malaysia-registered trailer was foiled after the contraband was found hidden beneath a load of concrete piles.
The Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) of Singapore said the trailer was stopped for further inspection at the Tuas Checkpoint on Sept 4 after officers detected anomalies in the scan images of the heavy vehicle.
"Further inspection uncovered 4,500 cartons of duty-unpaid cigarettes hidden beneath the load of concrete piles.
"Its 26-year-old Malaysian driver was arrested in connection with the case," it said in a statement.
ICA said the driver and seized cigarettes were subsequently handed over to Singapore Customs for further investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bersatu still has strength despite member exits, says Youth chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu remains relevant and retains influence through its representatives in Parliament and state assemblies despite defections by grassroots members, says Bersatu Youth chief Muhammad Hilman Idham.
He said the party, led by former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, would contest the upcoming Melaka election.
However, whether Bersatu will contest independently or cooperate with another coalition is expected to be announced by Muhyiddin on Saturday.
"Political parties must contest, but it is still too early to finalise anything. The state assembly has yet to be dissolved and discussions are ongoing.
"We are discussing whether to cooperate with other coalitions or go solo. There may be an important message from the president during Bersatu's 10th anniversary celebration on Saturday," he told Berita Harian here.
Earlier, Melaka Bersatu Youth chief Jefri Safry proposed that the party cooperate with Barisan Nasional (BN) and open discussions with the coalition ahead of the state election.
Jefri reportedly said a more open and pragmatic approach was needed to ensure Bersatu could face the election in a more organised manner.
Hilman, who is also Gombak Setia assemblyman, said Bersatu remained a member of Perikatan Nasional (PN), allowing it to contest under the coalition's banner.
He said Bersatu continued to have strength, with six members of Parliament and 12 state assemblymen in Selangor, despite reports of members leaving the party to join Wawasan.
"How many have left? Wawasan is also being shunned by Umno and Pas," he said.
Several reports have emerged of Bersatu members leaving the party, with the latest involving Kuala Kangsar Bersatu division deputy chief Datuk Adly Shah Ahmad Tah, who reportedly announced last Friday that he was relinquishing his position and leaving the party.
Adly Shah was joined by members from nine of the division's 11 branches, involving 115 members and party leaders.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Stray elephant safely relocated from Terengganu to Royal Belum State Park
Article:
HULU TERENGGANU: A male elephant that had wandered into Kampung Kolam, Ajil, here, last week was safely relocated to Royal Belum State Park this morning.
Terengganu Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) director Dennis Ten Choon Yung said the wild elephant was captured last Thursday before being relocated today.
He said the operation began at 9am and involved 24 personnel from Terengganu Perhilitan and the National Elephant Conservation Centre (PKGK) in Kuala Gandah.
The relocation proceeded smoothly, with the elephant successfully loaded onto a lorry at 11.30am for transportation to its release site.
"However, coaxing the elephant took some time as it was a wild animal, and the safety of personnel had to be prioritised.
"Two trained elephants, Sanum and Abot, both from PKGK Kuala Gandah, were used to assist in the relocation," he said.
Dennis said the elephant remained safe and stable throughout the operation before being transported to Royal Belum State Park for release.
He said the operation was part of Perhilitan's efforts to manage human-elephant conflict in Terengganu.
He added that 10 elephant relocation operations involving human-elephant conflicts had been carried out in Terengganu so far this year.
"The efforts are aimed at protecting public property and assets while ensuring the safety of residents when the presence of wild elephants poses a risk to humans," he said.
Meanwhile, more than 1,000 residents gathered in the area from early this morning to watch the elephant's relocation.
Residents said crowds had been visiting the area continuously since Thursday after the elephant was spotted wandering around Kampung Kolam.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar calls urgent meeting tomorrow to address higher electricity bills [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will hold a special meeting tomorrow to examine immediate measures to ease the impact of rising electricity bills on affected households.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the meeting would involve the Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry, Energy Commission, Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) and Finance Ministry.
He said the government had taken note of public concerns over higher electricity bills in recent weeks and that the matter needed to be addressed promptly.
"Upon returning from India and the Maldives, my attention immediately turned to concerns raised by the people regarding the recent increase in electricity bills.
"I have heard the concerns being raised, and this matter needs to be given attention and addressed immediately," he said in a statement today.
Anwar said the government remained committed to targeted subsidies to ensure most domestic consumers remained protected.
He said about 80 per cent of domestic users consuming no more than 600 kilowatt-hours (kWh) a month remained protected from rate increases linked to higher fuel costs.
However, haze and hotter weather in recent weeks had caused some households to increase their electricity consumption beyond the 600kWh threshold, making them subject to the Automatic Fuel Cost Adjustment (AFA), he said.
"Therefore, the Madani government will hold a special meeting tomorrow with the Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry, Energy Commission, TNB and Finance Ministry to examine immediate mitigation measures to reduce the impact of higher electricity bills on affected households," he said.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the government would continue to ensure targeted subsidy measures were implemented fairly and reasonably, with the people's welfare remaining a priority.
TNB yesterday clarified that
AFA
did not by itself cause sudden increases in electricity bills, following concerns raised by some consumers.
In a statement, the national utility company said AFA was a two-way mechanism that adjusted electricity charges according to changes in fuel costs and foreign exchange rates.
When fuel costs fall, consumers receive a rebate, while increases in fuel costs result in a surcharge.
TNB said the surcharge had been imposed since May following the crisis in the Middle East.
The AFA surcharge for September stood at 3.67 sen per kWh, it said.
Since AFA was introduced, consumers have received RM3.1 billion in rebates compared with RM800 million in surcharges, TNB said.
Consumers with monthly electricity consumption of 600kWh or less are fully exempt from AFA charges, whether rebates or surcharges apply.
They are also exempt from the eight per cent service tax and retail charges.
Under the new tariff, consumers in this category pay about two to 14 per cent less than under the previous tariff, depending on their level of consumption, TNB added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Every Malaysian has a role in defending country, says Khaled
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Every Malaysian has a role to play in defending the country, including by safeguarding unity and resisting elements that seek to divide society.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said national defence was not solely the responsibility of the military, as citizens also had a role to play.
"Today, we not only celebrate Malaysia Day, but also commemorate another important day for the country – the 93rd Armed Forces Day.
"We may not need to take up arms, but every citizen has a role to play in the defence of the country.
"Preserve our unity, strengthen the spirit of patriotism, do not be easily influenced by elements that seek to divide us, and continue to stand behind our servicemen and women," he said in a Facebook post.
Khaled said the peace and sovereignty enjoyed by Malaysians today were not achieved on their own, but were the result of the courage, loyalty and dedication of those who remained ready to defend the country.
"My highest appreciation goes to all armed forces personnel and veterans for their service, dedication and sacrifices for the motherland.
"The peace and sovereignty we enjoy today did not come on their own.
"Behind them are the courage, loyalty and dedication of those who are always ready to defend the country," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: 'Prime ministers come and go, but country must be saved'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has appealed to Malaysians to give his administration more time to pursue reforms, acknowledging public impatience over the pace of change while warning that faster action could trigger greater political resistance.
Addressing those who feel his administration's progress has fallen short of expectations, Anwar acknowledged his shortcomings but said his Cabinet was pushing ahead with reforms despite difficult circumstances.
"First, I have done the best I could. I apologise if it does not satisfy those who feel that it needs to be expedited.
"But you must understand, expediting action also invites hostility, as is happening now," Anwar said in a podcast, SembangOhhYeahh, which aired today.
Anwar said accelerating reforms risked provoking intense resistance from entrenched interests seeking to preserve the status quo.
"There are people who do not want any action, do not want any disclosure and do not want the word 'sakau' (embezzlement) to be used. They still exist.
"But I am grateful to those who have given their trust, and I want to appeal from the bottom of my heart to give us a chance to save our country," he said.
Acknowledging that prime ministers "come and go", Anwar said the priority was to safeguard Malaysia's standing and future potential.
"As I have said, prime ministers come and go, and I am mindful of that (in BM: saya insaf akan hal itu). But the country must be saved."
He pointed to the enthusiasm shown by young Malaysians during recent National Day celebrations as evidence of their optimism and confidence in the country's future.
"Malaysia has extraordinary potential. Young people, whether at universities or working in the public service, show their awareness and their interest.
"Just look at the way they celebrate our Independence Day. With great enthusiasm, with very high hopes."
Anwar said Malaysia must build on its progress rather than return to practices and attitudes that could undermine the country's strength.
"Do not turn back, look back and regress backwards. This country must move forward and at the level we have achieved now, we are respected in the region and in the world. Do not waste this opportunity.
"Do not allow us to return to practices and a culture of hatred towards people, hatred towards races and being more willing to accept corruption and abuse.
"This country has strength. Do not destroy it. That is what I hope for."
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said he remained open to criticism and acknowledged that there were shortcomings that could be addressed.
"I am open to criticism and I have been criticised a lot. I am the prime minister who has gone down to universities the most, engaging in dialogue with the young people. I can improve whatever I consider to be shortcomings and weaknesses.
"But I want to appeal, do not allow this country to be let down by a group whose interests could destroy our own strength."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three houses destroyed in Alor Star fire
Article:
ALOR STAR: Three houses along Jalan Stadium here were destroyed in a fire last night.
The Kedah Fire and Rescue Department operations centre received an emergency call regarding the incident at 9.40pm.
It said a team of 10 firefighters from the Alor Star Fire and Rescue Station, assisted by 54 personnel from nine nearby voluntary fire brigades, arrived at the scene to extinguish the blaze.
"Upon arrival, the operations commander reported that the fire involved three houses, comprising two Class B two-storey houses and one Class C single-storey house.
"All three houses were 90 per cent destroyed, but no victims were involved in the incident.
"The fire was brought under control at 10.10pm. The cause of the fire and the total losses are still under investigation," it said.
Overhaul operations were carried out at the site before the fire was completely extinguished, and the operation ended at 11.59pm.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chinese investors rush into US stocks as Beijing opens wider path overseas
Article:
SHANGHAI: Chinese investors are piling into foreign assets, especially US stock funds, after regulators lifted outbound quotas, unlocking pent-up demand as domestic yields are at rock bottom and Beijing tightens unofficial routes for moving money abroad.
While China has cracked down on what it deems illegal overseas investing through online brokerages, it has simultaneously broadened authorised channels to foreign markets.
Late last month China's foreign exchange regulator raised the outstanding Qualified Domestic Institutional Investor quota by US$6.8 billion to a record US$183 billion. The speed with which US-focused funds moved to curb inflows just days later underscores investors' scramble for exposure to Wall Street.
The daily inflow cap on a QDII fund tracking the Nasdaq 100 was raised from 10 yuan to 5,000 yuan on September 9. Just a day later, its fund manager Wanjia Asset Management sharply limited inflows again to 100 yuan daily for an individual investor.
"It means there was explosive inflows so the fund manager needed to limit the subscriptions," said Ivan Shi, head of research at fund consultancy Z-Ben Advisors. "There remains huge appetite in China for US tech stocks."
The rush overseas highlights Beijing's growing challenge in stemming capital outflows. Confidence in the domestic economy remains fragile, China's 10-year government bond yield sits more than three percentage points below US Treasury yields, and the local stock market has broadly lagged the double-digit gains delivered by US equities this year.
Portfolio investment hit a record US$426 billion deficit in 2025, according to China's Balance of Payments data, and net outflows reached US$146 billion in the first quarter of this year.
In another case, China Universal Asset Management eased restrictions on its Nasdaq 100 ETF, only to tighten curbs again two days later.  TruValue Asset Management took a similar U-turn on its QDII fund investing in global chip stocks.
"Chinese demand for global asset allocation is getting bigger and bigger," said Xu Jie, fund manager at Yuanzi Investment Management, which invests in global markets through exchange-traded funds (ETFs) under QDII.
Long-term investors need to "diversify risks and share growth in major global markets."
The US is the top destination for QDII funds, accounting for nearly half of the roughly 1 trillion yuan (US$150 billion) business, according to Shanghai Securities.
Most US-bound ETFs trade at a hefty premium to their net asset value, reflecting investors' eagerness to secure limited overseas exposure. A Shenzhen-listed ETF tracking the Nasdaq-100 Technology Sector Index traded at a premium of 24 per cent on Wednesday.
"The premium just reflects strong household demand on global assets," said Zhaopeng Xing, senior China strategist at ANZ.
China's balance of payments turned positive recently due to strong trade inflows, "but the regulators still need a balance to control outflows," he said.
(US$1 = 6.7131 Chinese yuan renminbi)
(Reporting by Shanghai newsroom; Editing by Tom Westbrook and Shri Navaratnam)
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysians in Jeddah and Makkah safe following Saudi emergency alert
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians in Jeddah and Makkah are safe following an emergency alert issued by Saudi Arabian authorities yesterday.
Malaysian Consul-General in Jeddah Tengku Mohd Dzaraif Raja Abdul Kadir said the consulate had distributed the official graphic issued by the Saudi Arabian Ministry of Interior to WhatsApp groups for Malaysians in the Hijazi region.
"Alhamdulillah, everything is fine in Jeddah and Makkah.
"We distributed the graphic from the Saudi Interior Ministry to WhatsApp groups for Malaysians in the Hijazi region.
"The important thing is for Malaysians not to panic. We also remind them not to share videos, as doing so is a major offence in Saudi Arabia," he said when contacted today.
Yesterday, Saudi Arabia issued a "
potential danger
" emergency alert for Jeddah, Makkah, and Taif in the western part of the country, urging residents to seek shelter and adhere to official safety instructions.
Citing reports from Anadolu Agency, the Saudi National Early Warning Platform for Emergencies urged residents to take shelter and follow official safety directives.
The warning was issued amid escalating clashes between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi group in Yemen, following a series of missile and drone attacks launched by the group.
Meanwhile, Qasswa Travel and Tours (M) Sdn Bhd chairman Datuk Mohd Najib Alwi said the agency is proceeding with planned umrah pilgrimages as no cancellations have been issued by the Saudi Ministry of Haj and Umrah.
"Our agency operates on umrah visas, and there are no cancellations to date. If the ministry cancels, we will comply.
"This may be the first time an alert has been issued. If it happens three times, we may need to reconsider. We will also monitor the situation and check with local muassasah for updates.
"At the same time, we will follow any advice issued by the Foreign Ministry," said Najib, who is scheduled to depart for umrah with a group of pilgrims on Sept 21.
He added that in the event of any cancellation, flight schedules and travel details would typically be rescheduled.
"Normally, my agency uses Malaysia Airlines and Turkish Airlines, both of which are very vigilant regarding ongoing developments and will cancel flights three to four days before departure if necessary.
"So far, my pilgrims understand the situation and the possibilities that may arise," he said.
Meanwhile, Wisma Putra, when asked to comment on the warning and subsequent measures, said it is closely monitoring developments.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia-China relations continue to flourish, expand into emerging sectors
Article:
BEIJING: Malaysia-China relations continue to flourish, with both countries committed to strengthening cooperation in trade, investment, technology and other high-potential areas, said Malaysia's Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad.
He said China remained an important partner for Malaysia, with bilateral ties based on mutual respect and trust continuing to produce positive results across various sectors over the 52 years since diplomatic relations were established.
"The relationship between Malaysia and China, which is based on mutual respect and trust, continues to grow from strength to strength," he said in his remarks at the Malaysia National Day Reception held at the China World Hotel.
Norman said China had remained Malaysia's largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, with total bilateral trade reaching US$132.50 billion (RM541.90 billion) in 2025, accounting for 17.7 per cent of Malaysia's total global trade.
He said bilateral trade continued to perform strongly this year, reaching US$35.49 billion (RM140.76 billion) from January to March 2026, while cumulative implemented investment from China between 1980 and 2025 stood at US$24.5 billion (RM110.9 billion).
"These implemented investments have created 106,712 jobs for the Malaysian people," he said, adding that Malaysia remained committed to attracting sustainable investments that would generate positive spillover effects for the national economy.
Norman said Malaysia also sought to expand cooperation with China in emerging and high-potential sectors, including technical and vocational education and training (TVET), the digital economy, artificial intelligence (AI) and green technology, in line with the New Industrial Master Plan 2030, the National Semiconductor Strategy and the Green Investment Strategy.
He said Malaysia, China and 36 other countries signed an agreement in July to become founding members of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organisation (WAICO), with Malaysia among seven Asean member states involved in its establishment.
"Malaysia stands committed to and fully supports WAICO's aims of promoting international cooperation and global governance on AI.
"We must ensure that AI is beneficial, safe, fair and open to all."
Norman said Malaysia welcomed China's initiatives, including the Belt and Road Initiative, Global Development Initiative, Global Security Initiative and Global Civilisation Initiative, while stressing the importance of an international environment based on equality and international law.
"For Malaysia and China, the only way forward is to move forward together.
"Malaysia stands ready to work hand in hand with our Chinese friends to build a better future for both our peoples," he said.
The reception, held in conjunction with Malaysia's 69th National Day and the 63rd anniversary of the formation of the Federation of Malaysia, was attended by 440 guests, including Chinese government representatives, members of the diplomatic corps, Malaysian Embassy officials, media practitioners, university students, industry players and Malaysians in Beijing.
Chinese Vice Foreign Minister Miao Deyu, who is also a member of the Communist Party of China Committee of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, was the guest of honour.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 200,000 residents oppose 17,000-unit Bukit Jalil apartment project
Article:
BUKIT JALIL: More than 200,000 residents from three housing areas here are opposing the proposed construction of 17,000 apartment units, citing concerns over worsening congestion and inadequate infrastructure.
Protest committee chairman Zainuddin Zainal said the opposition involved residents of Bukit Jalil, Bandar Kinrara and Taman Puncak Jalil.
He said residents were unanimously opposed to the high-density development, which they feared would worsen congestion in the area.
"The total population in these three housing areas is now 209,000 and is expected to increase by another 51,000 if the project goes ahead.
"At the same time, the existing infrastructure cannot cope with residents' current needs," he told reporters at a dialogue session on the proposed construction of 17,000 apartment units in Bukit Jalil today.
The large-scale housing project, planned for a 26-hectare site, is understood to comprise about 10 per cent affordable homes, with the remainder priced at more than RM360,000.
The developer had planned to begin the 17,000-unit apartment project in June this year, but it was postponed after failing to obtain approval from Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) following objections from residents.
Zainuddin said residents wanted the government to instead develop much-needed infrastructure, including schools, a hospital and Light Rail Transit (LRT) or Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) stations.
He said residents were informed of the development plans in January.
"We disagreed and began protesting, including gathering at the project site today with about 300 residents.
"We will submit a memorandum opposing the construction of the 17,000 apartment units to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim at Parliament in October.
"We hope our concerns will be heard for the well-being of residents," he said.
Resident Che Mazenah Che Omar, 58, said they were worried the development would worsen congestion, which she said was already close to paralysing traffic during peak hours.
"Traffic is already too heavy as early as 6.30am, forcing residents to leave early to get to work and send their children to school.
"If they leave home late to send their children to school or go to work, they can be stuck in traffic for almost 2 hours," she said.
She said residents also faced a shortage of schools, with schools in Bukit Jalil reportedly already unable to accommodate the number of students.
"Residents also have to send their children to schools some distance from their homes in Taman OUG and Bandar Kinrara.
"Residents also face difficulties getting treatment at Klinik Muhibah, Bukit Jalil, as there are too many patients, after which they are referred to Klinik Sungai Besi," she said.
As such, residents want basic facilities to be provided first to meet the needs of the existing population before any mega development is carried out.
